raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation On GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), a CUDA-graph decode replay spreads across many CUDA streams, so a profiler trace is hard to read: each layer's indexer chain lands on a different stream row. This is the same issue as DeepSeek-V4.1 in #39420. That PR found that at graph replay a join node continues on the stream of its first-recorded parent. A side-stream block captured before the concurrent main-stream kernels therefore pulls the main chain onto a side lane at the join. Its fix keeps the fork where it is and captures the side-stream work right before the join. Inspired by and following the approach of #39420 ("[DSV4.1] Record side-stream work right before its join"). ## Modifications Two side-stream blocks on the GLM-5.2 decode path were captured before the main-stream kernels they run alongside. In both, the fork (`alt_stream.wait_stream(current_stream)`) stays where it was, and only the capture order of the side block changes. 1. `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py`, `_fused_q_prepare_and_store`, stage 1: the `wq_b` GEMM on `alt_stream` is now captured after the main-stream `wk_weights_proj`, right before the join. 2. `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py` (decode graphs, DSA path): the `q_b_proj` block on `alt_stream` is now captured after the indexer, right before `current_stream.wait_stream(self.alt_stream)`. `k_nope.unsqueeze(1)`, a view with no kernel, now runs on the main stream. I checked the rest of the GLM-5.2 path and found no other active violation under TP4 / NVFP4 / `flashmla_kv`. In particular, `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal_dual_stream` already issues the routed experts before the shared-expert side block, and stage 2 of the fused indexer is already ordered correctly. Test: `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsa_indexer_stream_order.py` pins the issue order of the stage-1 block (fork, main GEMM, alt `wq_b`, join). It fails without the change and passes with it. ## Results GLM-5.2-NVFP4, aggregated serving, TP=4, CUDA graphs on, dummy weights, GB200 x4. One run per arm, rank TP1, same load for both. Distinct CUDA streams seen in the profiler trace: | | baseline | this PR | |---|---|---| | 10-step decode window | 123 | 81 | | 30 ms slice of the window | 45 | 3 | In the baseline, 99 of the 123 streams are tiny, each carrying a few kernels of the indexer chain (`fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_quant`, `sm100_paged_mqa_logits`, `topk_small_batch_cluster_kernel` and a TgvGemm kernel). With this PR those streams disappear: two main lanes carry about 13.3k and 9.8k kernels. The kernel count is identical (23,324 vs 23,319), so the same work runs. Median TPOT (`sglang.bench_serving`, random 512 in / 256 out): | concurrency | baseline | this PR | |---|---|---| | 1 | 10.51 ms | 10.43 ms | | 8 | 11.88 ms | 11.78 ms | | 16 | 13.33 ms | 13.28 ms | No regression. The 0.4% to 0.8% gain is within single-run noise and is not claimed as a speedup. ## Reproduce Model files only, no weights (config and tokenizer from `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`; weights are random via `--load-format dummy`): ```bash mkdir -p /path/to/glm52_cfg && cd /path/to/glm52_cfg for f in config.json generation_config.json hf_quant_config.json tokenizer.json tokenizer_config.json chat_template.jinja model.safetensors.index.json; do curl -sfL -O https://huggingface.co/nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4/resolve/main/$f done ``` Server (run once on `main` and once on this branch): ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /path/to/glm52_cfg --load-format dummy \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --max-running-requests 16 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 \ --context-length 32768 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` TPOT at concurrency 1, 8 and 16: ```bash for C in 1 8 16; do python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --model /path/to/glm52_cfg \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts $((C*4)) --max-concurrency $C --warmup-requests 2 --seed 1 done ``` Trace of a steady-state decode window (start profiling about 6 s into the run, while it is decoding): ```bash python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --model /path/to/glm52_cfg \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 16 --seed 2 & sleep 6 curl -s -X POST localhost:30000/start_profile -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"num_steps":10,"activities":["CPU","GPU"],"output_dir":"/path/to/trace","profile_prefix":"run"}' wait ``` Count distinct streams per rank: read the trace JSON, take events with `ph == "X"` and `cat == "kernel"`, and count the distinct `args.stream` values. The full traces are 330 to 460 MB each. For Perfetto, cut a 30 ms window from one rank so it loads. ## Notes and limits - Dummy weights: this checks stream layout and latency only. It says nothing about accuracy. I compared TPOT, not generated outputs. - Single run per arm, one rank analyzed. The TPOT difference is within noise. - Stream assignment at replay is driver behavior. The result is from one driver and torch version here (torch 2.14.1+cu130, driver 580.x). - The `forward_mla.py` edit moves `q_b_proj` after the indexer. A reviewer raised a theoretical allocator-reuse hazard: tensors the indexer allocates on `alt_stream` are freed at return, and the trailing `q_b_proj` could reuse a block while a main-stream kernel still reads it. I did not reproduce a failure, and the A/B shows no change in throughput. I have not proven it safe either, so please look at this one closely. - The patched trace still has 78 streams that each hold one kernel, a FlashInfer RMSNorm, one per layer. They come from a separate stream hop that this PR does not touch. - This covers the CUDA-graph decode path (`is_decode_or_idle`). The target-verify and draft-extend graphs do not take the `forward_mla.py` overlap branch. ## Checklist - [x] Unit test added - [ ] Accuracy test (not run; dummy weights) The diff is still uncommitted on glm52-graph-stream-fork, and nothing is pushed. Two things to decide before you post it: - Allocator-race note. I disclosed the unresolved allocator-race concern about the forward_mla.py edit in "Notes and limits". I'd leave it in; the alternative is dropping that edit or adding a keep-alive fix. - Repeat runs. Repeating each arm a few times would let you replace "within noise" with a number. Perfetto screenshots (30 ms slice, rank TP1): before PR: after PR: --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #39392800055](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39392800055) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39392800085](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39392800085) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #39392800119](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39392800119) cc. @nvpohanh @BBuf
